variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
val x = 10

(* Mutable reference *)
val y = ref 20
val _ = y := !y + 5
variables.notes: Bindings are created using 'val'. They are immutable. SML also supports explicit mutable cells using 'ref' and the assignment operator ':='.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
val i : int = 42
val f : real = 3.14
val b : bool = true
val c : char = #"X"
val s : string = "Hello"

(* Datatype definition *)
datatype shape = 
    Circle of real
  | Rectangle of real * real
data_types.notes: SML has strong static typing with type inference. Floating-point numbers are called 'real'. Characters have a special #"c" syntax.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
val add_int = 5 + 3
val add_real = 5.0 + 3.0

val div_int = 5 div 2
val div_real = 5.0 / 2.0
val rem_int = 5 mod 2

val logic = true andalso (not false) orelse true

val eq = (5 = 5)
val neq = (5 <> 3)
operators.notes: Operators are overloaded for 'int' and 'real', but type inference needs context or annotations if ambiguous. 'andalso' and 'orelse' are short-circuiting.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
val result = 
  if x > 0 then
    "Positive"
  else
    "Non-positive"

(* Pattern matching in case expression *)
val sign = case x of
    _ => if x > 0 then 1 else if x < 0 then ~1 else 0
conditionals.notes: if-then-else must have both branches returning the same type. There are no guard clauses in SML pattern matching like in Haskell, so if-expressions are used inside.

for_loop.title: For Loop (Recursion/Map)
for_loop.code:
(* SML has no for loop. Iterate via recursion or map *)
val lst = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
val squares = List.map (fn x => x * x) lst

fun loop_print 0 = ()
  | loop_print n = (
      print (Int.toString n ^ "\n");
      loop_print (n - 1)
    )
for_loop.notes: Iteration is idiomatic through higher-order functions like List.map and List.foldl, or direct recursion.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: SML provides an imperative 'while' loop. It relies on evaluating a boolean condition and side effects (like updating refs).

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
fun add x y = x + y

(* Pattern matching in arguments *)
fun factorial 0 = 1
  | factorial n = n * factorial (n - 1)

(* Anonymous function *)
val multiply = fn x => fn y => x * y
functions.notes: Functions are defined using 'fun'. Multiple clauses allow elegant pattern matching directly in the function definition.

arrays.title: Arrays and Lists
arrays.code:
(* List (immutable) *)
val lst = [1, 2, 3]
val new_lst = 0 :: lst

(* Array (mutable) *)
val arr = Array.fromList [1, 2, 3]
val _ = Array.update(arr, 0, 99)
val first = Array.sub(arr, 0)
arrays.notes: Lists use the '::' (cons) operator. Arrays are mutable data structures with sub/update functions.

maps.title: Maps (Using binary search trees)
maps.code:
(* Requires a structure definition, varies slightly by implementation like SML/NJ *)
structure IntMap = BinaryMapFn(struct
  type ord_key = int
  val compare = Int.compare
end)

val m = IntMap.empty
val m1 = IntMap.insert(m, 1, "apple")
val opt = IntMap.find(m1, 1)
maps.notes: Maps use functor instantiation over an ordered key type. The implementation depends on the specific SML compiler ecosystem.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
exception DivByZero

fun divide (x, 0) = raise DivByZero
  | divide (x, y) = x div y

val result = 
  divide (10, 0) handle DivByZero => 0

(* Option type *)
fun safe_div (x, 0) = NONE
  | safe_div (x, y) = SOME (x div y)
error_handling.notes: Exceptions are raised and caught with 'handle'. Option types (NONE/SOME) are heavily used for pure functional error handling.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
-- Single-line comment
{- Multi-line
   comment block -}
add :: Int -> Int -> Int
add a b = a + b
comments.notes: Standard ML uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Standard ML supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.notes: Standard ML treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: Standard ML performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.notes: Standard ML represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.code:
import Text.Printf
msg = printf "User %s scored %d" "Alice" (95 :: Int)
string_formatting.notes: Standard ML formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Standard ML, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.notes: Standard ML constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.code: for x <- 1..10, rem(x, 2) == 0, do: x * x
iterators.notes: Standard ML achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.code:
defmodule Person do
  defstruct [:name, :age]
  def greet(%Person{name: name}), do: "Hello #{name}"
end
oop_classes.notes: Standard ML emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.notes: Lists in Standard ML are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Standard ML uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.notes: Standard ML provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.code:
defmodule MyModule do
  import Enum, only: [map: 2]
  alias MyProject.Helper
end
modules_import.notes: Standard ML isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
